audit_findings.title: Modeled growth may belong partly to future shareholders
audit_findings.magnitude: future impact unquantified; approximately 0.6 million shares issued under the DRIP/DSPP and ATM programs reduced first-half 2026 EPS by $0.12, while 2025 and first-half 2026 equity proceeds were $123.0 million and $16.8 million
audit_findings.mechanism: The model grows total OE by 7%–9% while holding the 24.428455 million-share denominator fixed; equity financing increases shares and debt financing increases interest retained in equity-level OE.
audit_findings.evidence: Our business strategy includes the continued pursuit of growth and requires capital investment in excess of cash flow from operations.
audit_findings.explanation: External financing is demonstrably part of the growth model, and recent filings show recurring issuance and measurable dilution. The future funding mix is unknown, but the issue is reasonably capable of materially reducing per-share growth because the modeled base case is $30.87 per share above the zero-growth bear case.
audit_findings.action: Build annual debt and equity funding schedules for modeled capital expenditures, forecast diluted shares and interest expense, and rerun all scenarios using per-share OE growth after financing.

audit_findings.title: The historical trend crosses an acquisition and share-count discontinuity
audit_findings.magnitude: valuation effect unquantified; the filed discontinuity comprises a $922.8 million acquisition financed partly by 4.4 million new shares
audit_findings.mechanism: The discontinuity enters the $134.3 million trend-derived OE anchor and any growth inference drawn from total OE, while the associated share issuance changes the ownership claim represented by each share.
audit_findings.evidence: Weighted average shares reflect the impact of 4.4 million common shares issued in November 2023 in connection with the acquisition of FCG.
audit_findings.explanation: The perimeter and share-count break is demonstrated, but the record does not provide comparable-perimeter OE needed to measure the anchor error. The fact that the selected anchor is below 2025 OE does not establish that the fitted trend is valid; a recast could move the normalized anchor in either direction.
audit_findings.action: Reconstruct OE per diluted share by year and recast pre-2024 results for FCG or separately model legacy organic OE, acquired OE, acquisition financing and dilution; then refit the anchor and rerun the valuation.

audit_findings.title: Net regulatory customer obligations are absent from the bridge
audit_findings.magnitude: $127.1 million latest net regulatory liability, computed as $219.6 million of June 2026 regulatory liabilities less $92.5 million of regulatory assets; $5.20 per share and 5.4% of the $2,353 million base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Any portion not already reflected through future regulated revenue, expense or normalized OE would enter either the equity bridge as a customer claim or forecast OE through refunds, rate reductions and recoveries.
audit_findings.evidence: These assets and liabilities will be recognized as revenues and expenses in future periods as they are reflected in customers’ rates.
audit_findings.explanation: The balances require mapping, but deducting the entire latest net balance as an immediate equity claim—an intentionally conservative treatment—would reduce base value to about $91.10 per share and bull value to about $102.21 per share. Both remain below the $132.66 market price, so this finding cannot change the current valuation conclusion. Moreover, several balances are timing mechanisms or future removal costs rather than debt-like claims.
audit_findings.action: Map each material regulatory asset and liability to its amortization, refund, recovery and rate-base treatment; rerun only if that work identifies an unembedded burden, while preventing double counting against forecast OE.

audit_findings.title: The 2025 OE point may retain non-recurring asset-sale gains
audit_findings.magnitude: $10.6 million pretax; approximately $7.7 million after applying the filed 27.3% effective tax rate; a log-trend sensitivity reduces the anchor by approximately $2.6 million, or 1.9%, and base value by about $1.83 per share
audit_findings.mechanism: If retained, the gains inflate the 2025 OE observation and, through that observation, the fitted log-trend anchor used in every scenario.
audit_findings.evidence: The increase in 2025 was largely attributable to higher gains on asset sales compared to the prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: The gain is demonstrated, but its retention in OE is not. Even assuming the full $10.6 million was retained, taxing it at the filed effective rate and refitting the supplied log trend produces only an approximately 1.9% valuation reduction. Base value would remain roughly $94.47 per share versus the $132.66 price, so the conclusion would not change.
audit_findings.action: Trace the OE reconciliation to the realized-gain line, identify any commodity-contract component or customer sharing, remove the applicable after-tax non-recurring amount, and preserve the sensitivity calculation in the valuation record.

audit_findings.title: A pending appeal could impair FCG rate economics
audit_findings.magnitude: $0 incremental downside from this appeal after the June 2026 ruling; FCG's filed 2025 net income was $5.2 million for scale
audit_findings.mechanism: An adverse ruling could have reduced FCG OE or created a refund liability, but the latest filing states that the Florida Supreme Court ruled against the Florida OPC on all contested matters.
audit_findings.evidence: The Florida Supreme Court has yet to rule on the case.
audit_findings.explanation: The appeal was pending in the 2025 filing but was resolved in the company's favor before the valuation date. Consequently, the specific reversal, remand and refund pathway identified by this finding is no longer open and contributes no adverse valuation adjustment.
audit_findings.action: Retain the June 2026 court disposition in the evidence file and make no rerun for this appeal; assess the separate 2026 FCG rate case on its own facts.

audit_findings.title: Capitalized construction interest weakens the interest-retention premise
audit_findings.magnitude: $1.6 million disclosed year-over-year increment, equal to 1.2% of the $134.3 million anchor; if sustained and entirely omitted, approximately $28 million or $1.15 per share of base value
audit_findings.mechanism: Capitalized interest avoids current interest expense while growth capex is excluded from OE, temporarily overstating OE unless the financing cost is incorporated into growth funding or subsequently captured without double counting.
audit_findings.evidence: Increased interest expense was partially offset by lower average outstanding Revolver borrowings, a lower weighted-average interest rate, and higher capitalized interest of $1.6 million associated with growth capital projects compared to the prior year.
audit_findings.explanation: The accounting mismatch is demonstrated for the disclosed increment, but its present scale is insufficient to change the conclusion: even an aggressive assumption that the entire $1.6 million is a continuing annual OE omission affects base value by only about $1.15 per share versus the $36.36 gap between base value and market price. Larger future capitalization remains a forward-looking monitoring issue.
audit_findings.action: Reconcile total cash interest to expensed and capitalized interest annually, incorporate capitalized financing costs into the growth-funding schedule, and rerun if the cumulative omitted amount becomes materially larger than the disclosed $1.6 million increment.
